checks: Verified source 5c1f3bb21840ea60 §4 (9) and de0cd073e31eb7f8 §1 at the declared digests. The pencil uses the same planes after scaling with p=z/x, q=z/y (ordered to have p<q) and p+q=(1−2z)/(1+z). Its third raw representative has the opposite orientation.

The discriminant is 1−8z>0 and both the product and sum of roots are positive throughout 0<z<1/8, so both diagonal points are interior and x≠y. The third diagonal point also has positive entries summing to one. Neither first point has equal first two entries.

Substituting the root equation gives (1+z+x)(x+z)=2x, so 3λ₀=1+z. The corresponding relation for y, negative-pair symmetry and the centroid sum give (A,A,B,B). In the third plane all crossing coordinate sums are A+B=1/2, so the centroid equals its diagonal point. The diagonal bijection gives distinct unoriented planes.

At z=3/25 the discriminant is 1/25 and the roots are 12/25 and 7/25. Reciprocal heights are proportional to the listed vectors, and independent exact determinants and triangle area weighting give the common centroid (56,56,19,19)/150, fractions 4/25 and moments −111/400 for the first two caps.
For all displayed z, A>1/3. The claim concerns unrestricted centroid inversion in one split and gives no central-region inverse counterexample.
